title: Make the answer easier to understand.
summary: Start with clear prose. Add a diagram when relationships matter. Build an interactive page when the user needs to explore an explanation.

sections.title: Choose the format for the question

blocks.text: The goal is to reduce the reader's effort. A short answer may be enough. A complex decision may need a page that combines prose, a diagram, and evidence.

blocks.caption: Choose the format that helps the user understand this particular question. More elaborate output is useful only when it adds clarity.

data.title: Match the format to the question
data.description: Start with the user's question. Use prose for a brief answer, a diagram for relationships, or an HTML page for exploration. Check whether the result is easy to understand.

nodes.label: What does the user need to understand?
Check the result with the user's question in mind

sections.title: Explain one idea at a time

blocks.title: From a result to an explanation

items.title: State the answer
items.text: Lead with the conclusion the user needs. Example: use a queue to absorb short bursts of work.

items.title: Show the mechanism
items.text: A producer adds work to the queue. A worker takes one task when it has capacity. A sequence diagram can show this exchange.

items.title: Name the limit
items.text: A queue delays work when demand exceeds capacity. It does not create capacity. State the expected load before recommending a queue size.

blocks.summary: What does relaxed ASD-STE100 mean here?

blocks.text: Use short sentences, stable terms, active verbs, and one main idea at a time. Keep technical precision. This skill borrows writing principles; it does not certify compliance with the standard.
Instead of: The implementation leverages asynchronous orchestration. Write: The worker runs several tasks at once.

blocks.caption: This simplified queue example shows the order of messages. It omits retries and failures so the basic exchange is easy to see.

data.title: A producer, queue, and worker
data.description: The producer submits a task to the queue. The worker requests a task. The queue returns one task, and the worker reports completion.

sections.title: Keep the tools close to the skill

blocks.text: Install the writing directory under an OpenCode skills directory. The agent loads the skill, reads the tool reference, and runs the bundled scripts through shell.
